title: Conclusions Engine Batch 001 — Public Power Findings
mission: Convert tracking feed data into defensible public conclusions: what is proven by public records, what is strongly indicated, what is open, what is missing, and what cannot be claimed yet.
boundary: This engine does not declare guilt or hidden intent. It produces evidence-grade conclusions from public-record source routes, company filings, regulator lanes, public-contract routes, transparency reports, and missing-record pressure lists.
conclusionRules: A conclusion can be published when it is supported by a public source route or verified record card.
A public-power conclusion is not a legal accusation.
A missing-record conclusion means the record is required before upgrading a claim.
Intent, hidden coordination, corruption, or unlawful conduct require direct legal or verified records.
Sensitive records are linked or marked gated; they are not reproduced.

findings.title: The site now has a working power-tracking model.
findings.conclusion: Matrix Reprogrammed can track high-power people and institutions by public-record infrastructure lanes: AI, cloud, social platforms, satellites, public-sector data systems, finance, health data, identity/payment systems, and information ranking.
findings.doesNotMean: It does not mean every listed person is guilty of a crime or operating a proven unlawful plan.
findings.nextAction: Convert source routes into verified record cards.

findings.title: The first top-ten target list is data-driven and updateable.
findings.conclusion: The top-ten power targets are stored in JSON and rendered into public pages, meaning the ranking can change when evidence or scoring data changes.
findings.doesNotMean: It does not freeze the ranking forever or prove the list is complete.
findings.nextAction: Add scoring values, source dates and last-reviewed fields to every target.

findings.title: The public-record intake lanes are defined.
findings.conclusion: The tracker now has source lanes for SEC/annual reports, public contracts, transparency reports, regulators, privacy-impact assessments, lobbying/political-money records and missing-record pressure.
findings.doesNotMean: It does not prove each record has already been pulled or verified.
findings.nextAction: Create verified source cards for each top-ten target's first SEC or official source route.

findings.title: The core architecture to watch is bigger than one case.
findings.conclusion: Epstein files remain one major investigation lane, but the broader site mission now includes the modern power architecture: AI compute, cloud, platform data, space/telecom, finance, public-sector systems and missing records.
findings.doesNotMean: It does not claim all power-architecture targets are tied to Epstein.
findings.nextAction: Keep Epstein lanes separate from general power-architecture lanes unless source records connect them.

findings.title: The most urgent next evidence job is record conversion.
findings.conclusion: The site has enough structure. The next value comes from pulling and classifying source records into verified cards, especially SEC filings, public-contract routes, transparency reports, regulator records and court PDFs.
findings.doesNotMean: It does not mean the site is finished or every tracker is full.
findings.nextAction: Run TRACK-FEED-002: first verified source cards for the top ten.

findings.title: Intent claims remain open until direct records support them.
findings.conclusion: The site can track who has capacity to shape major public systems, but it cannot responsibly conclude personal intent or coordinated hidden action without direct source records.
findings.doesNotMean: It does not deny the possibility of coordination; it means the current evidence model keeps those claims in open/missing lanes.
findings.nextAction: Build a Claims Board with claim, supporting records, counter-sources and falsification tests.

publicSummary: The system is now ready to operate as an evidence machine. It can track power architecture, expose missing records, and create public conclusions only when source routes support them. The next step is record conversion: first source cards, then verified record cards, then upgraded conclusions.
